teardown_report.what: During a visible demo of this branch at d953aa3d, Quick Deck's window went away while the shell stayed up; the demo's log has exactly 'wm: removing client 1' then 'wm: module instance card.1 torn down; isolate SplashVmId(1) freed', after two Present renders of the slide with a video, and nothing else
teardown_report.signature: that pair is the shell's ordinary close (crates/shell/src/lib.rs close_client → remove_client → module_host.rs teardown). A module fault logs 'wm: contained a module panic in isolate …' (module_host.rs:114) and leaves the tile with a failure until 'failed module instance … released' (module_host.rs:1219); a script error logs [E] splash lines; a Video error logs 'Error decoding video with id …' (video.rs:1874). None of these is in the demo's log
teardown_report.reproduced: In a hidden macOS shell (the demo's binary on a copy of the demo profile; the deck, its frames and logs stayed on that Mac and are not in this evidence), Cmd+W gave exactly the demo's two lines (crates/shell/src/binds.rs:151-152: Super+W and Super+Q are Close window, and Super is Cmd on macOS). Playing the deck's video from the canvas control and the inspector, pausing, tapping it, changing slides while it played, Present with six taps on the clip, the arrow keys, Space, Escape and Return in Present, and browsing every slide closed nothing
teardown_report.conclusion: a close request, not a crash: Cmd+W or Cmd+Q (Close window in the shell), the window's close button, or a right or middle click on the bar's window title. Present can't be left with Escape (script apps get no key events), so a presenter's next reflex closes the app. Not an app bug; the shell could log which input closed a client, and Splash apps can't ask before a close (App Hub's card runner answers close_requested with Allow), so a close also drops unsaved edits

toolbar_rename: Quick Deck's toolbar region is now `qd_toolbar`, not `bar`: on main since #516 the shell's `self.ui.widget(cx, ids!(bar))` found an app's `bar` first and panicked ('value belongs to a different heap'); #519 fixes the shell, and the model test quick_deck_names_no_widget_the_shell_finds_by_name_in_its_window keeps Quick Deck off every name the shell looks up in its window.
